papers.title: MLAFormer: Multi-scale transformer with local convolutional auto-correlation and pre-training for time series forecasting
papers.authors: Jin Y., Gao M., Tang J., Fan W., Yang Y., An J.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based models have achieved strong performance in long-term time series forecasting, yet they often struggle to jointly model short-term local patterns and long-range dependencies under a unified representation, especially when temporal dynamics vary across different resolutions. To address this challenge, we propose MLAFormer, a multi-scale encoder-decoder framework for long-sequence forecasting. MLAFormer learns temporal representations across multiple resolutions through a cross multi-scale architecture, enabling information exchange between fine-grained and coarse-grained temporal features. In addition, we propose a Local Convolutional Auto-correlation mechanism to enhance local contextual modeling while capturing periodic dependencies efficiently. To further improve representation quality, we incorporate self-supervised pre-training within the encoder-decoder framework and investigate different masking strategies for time series reconstruction. Extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets demonstrate that MLAFormer consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in long-term forecasting. On average, MLAFormer reduces MAE by 7.4% compared with the recent advanced model, with an additional 3.0% improvement through pre-training.

papers.title: Fair client selection for multi-task federated learning in mobile edge networks
papers.authors: Su L., Guo J., Liu J., Liu X.
papers.abstract: Multi-task federated learning (FL) in mobile edge networks faces significant challenges due to the coexistence of heterogeneous tasks, dynamic client states, and limited computational resources. Most existing client selection methods often assume a single-task scenario with prior knowledge of client conditions, making them unsuitable for real-world multi-task training. Moreover, a critical issue is fairness: if resource-abundant devices are consistently favored, weaker clients may be excluded, leading to biased global models and lower training performance. To bridge this gap, we propose multi-task client selection MTC, a novel online algorithm that reformulates the selection process as a multi-agent multi-armed bandit (MAMAB) problem with proportional fairness constraints. MTC operates in rounds, each comprising four stages-exploration, mapping, exploitation, and rounding-enabling it to learn client performance while ensuring efficient and fair resource allocation. Theoretically, MTC can achieve both sub-linear regret and computational efficiency. Empirically, extensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that MTC not only improves accuracy by up to 2% to 26% over state-of-the-art baselines (EffI-FL, EMAFL, Fair-CFL, and FedProx), but also significantly enhances fairness-ensuring that even resource-constrained devices contribute to training. These results highlight the practical value of fair client selection for robust FL in real-world mobile edge networks.

papers.title: How to teach and forget: Towards cross-modal semantic consistency for entity alignment
papers.authors: Wang C., Miao C., Hu P., Wang W., Bao F.
papers.abstract: Multimodal Entity Alignment (MEA) aims to match identical entities across Multimodal Knowledge Graphs (MMKGs) by integrating complementary information from different modalities, such as visual and structure. In practice, MEA is complicated by two issues. Within a single MMKG, different modalities describing the same entity may not align well semantically. Across different MMKGs, the same entity may be associated with inconsistent or incomplete modality information, even within the same modality type. To address these challenges, we propose TeFo, a novel framework designed to enhance cross-modal semantic consistency by Teaching and Forgetting. Specifically, we introduce the Adaptive Modality Distillation module to teach. It aggregates semantic signals from multiple modalities to construct a modality-aware teacher representation. This teacher helps align each single-modality student toward a unified semantic space, which in turn alleviates inter-graph heterogeneity. Furthermore, we design the Gated Adversarial Alignment module to forget. It combines a gated feature selector and a modality discriminator trained with gradient reversal to reduce modality-specific variation. This encourages TeFo to rely less on modality-specific cues, and implicitly improves its robustness to modality asymmetry. Extensive experiments on nine public datasets show that TeFo significantly surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods, yielding absolute gains of 1.9%-2.3% in Hits@1 and 1.4%-2.4% in MRR. Our code is available at https://github.com/wonderCS1213/TeFo.

papers.title: CTJANet: A class-task joint-aware network for enhanced few-shot image classification
papers.authors: Sun Z., Wang M., Zhang X., Guo P.
papers.abstract: Few-shot image classification remains challenging due to the difficulty of recognizing novel categories from limited labeled samples. While recent methods employ information-aware strategies, they often depend on a single type of perceptual cue, missing the benefits of integrating multiple perspectives. To overcome this limitation, we propose a CTJANet (Class-Task Joint-Aware Network), which jointly leverages class-aware and task-aware cues for enhanced feature representation. Furthermore, we introduce a Task Adaptive-Aware Module (TAAM) that dynamically extracts task-specific embeddings through task-aware functions, improving adaptability to diverse tasks. Extensive experiments show that CTJANet outperforms the baseline FewTURE by significant margins: +5.29% (1-shot) and +3.74% (5-shot) on mini-ImageNet, +4.98% (1-shot) and +4.12% (5-shot) on tiered-ImageNet, +3.00% (1-shot) and +1.54% (5-shot) on CIFAR-FS, and +3.90% (1-shot) and +3.58% (5-shot) on FC100. Ablation studies also confirm the superiority of CTJANet, maintaining high classification accuracy and strong generalization. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/xiaozhugongqang/ZitWMY.

papers.title: Extracting policy attention from Chinese texts: An LLM-enhanced dynamic topic modeling approach for the “Dual Carbon” agenda
papers.authors: Guo Y., Yu S., Fu M., Jiang C.
papers.abstract: Extracting dynamic policy attention from large-scale Chinese policy texts remains challenging due to limitations in semantic representation and temporal modeling. This study proposes a Chinese-Prompt Dynamic Topic Model (CPDTM) that integrates Chinese pretrained language models with large language model–based prompt engineering to systematically link governmental attention allocation to governance outcomes. Taking 3056 “dual carbon” policy documents issued between October 2020 and June 2024 as an example, CPDTM achieves the best performance in topic quality. Our experiments identify the evolving policy attention in four key domains: ecological and meteorological development, green and low-carbon governance, industrial energy conservation and emission reduction, and technological innovation and development, showing a significant shift toward green and low-carbon governance. Furthermore, an autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) indicates that a 1% increase in long-run policy attention is associated with carbon emissions reductions of 0.5%, 0.3%, 0.2%, and 1.4% across these domains, while short-run effects vary substantially. Additionally, policy attention reduces carbon emissions through three primary channels: environmental governance constraints, green technology innovation, and industrial structure adjustment. This study contributes by (1) advancing dynamic topic modeling through LLM-enhanced prompting for large-scale Chinese policy texts, (2) uncovering the temporal evolution of “dual carbon” policy attention, and (3) providing empirical evidence on how information embedded in policy texts translates into emission outcomes, offering insights for policy optimization and sustainable governance.

papers.title: Legacy Learning Strategy Based on Few-Shot Font Generation Models for Automatic Text Design
papers.authors: Kim Y., Jeong S.C., Kim D., Sim S.
papers.abstract: Text design plays a vital role in enhancing user experience and maintaining visual coherence across digital platforms. However, for languages containing thousands of glyphs, creating new fonts remains costly and labor-intensive. Few-shot font generation (FFG) has emerged as a promising approach that synthesizes unseen glyphs from a small number of reference samples. Nevertheless, over 5–10% of glyphs must still be manually produced, limiting scalability. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes a plug-and-play legacy learning strategy that enhances both stylistic diversity and structural stability. The model-agnostic method performs iterative cross-font fine-tuning, progressively aligning the pretrained models' style representation toward a legacy-centric embedding space while introducing a content preservation loss to constrain geometric deformation and maintain glyph integrity. The proposed strategy was applied to five state-of-the-art FFG models and evaluated on large-scale Korean, Chinese and Thai font sets. Experimental results based on Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) similarity show that the generated glyphs gradually diverged from the original font distribution while converging toward the legacy font distribution, achieving stylistic variety with structural coherence. In addition, quantitative assessments of structural preservation and readability (Dice similarity, Chamfer distance, and OCR) confirm geometric stability without structural collapse. Cross-language and multilingual generalization was further verified, and a user study with 70 participants (experts and nonexperts) achieved average usability scores above 4.5/5. These results highlight legacy learning as an efficient and scalable strategy for automated, high-quality font generation in multilingual digital content environments.

papers.title: Dualmark: A novel dual watermarking approach for large language models
papers.authors: Qiang Z., Hao J., Qiang J., Zhu Y., Zhang C., Liu Y., Li W.
papers.abstract: Watermarking, which embeds imperceptible yet machine-detectable patterns into generated text, has emerged as a leading solution for detecting machine-generated content. While green-red watermarking methods embed detectable signals by biasing a “green” token subset, they remain vulnerable to paraphrasing attacks and context shifts: green tokens can be replaced, and edits to preceding tokens can disrupt the green-red partition. To address these limitations, we introduce DualMark, a novel ensemble-based dual-watermarking framework that employs an ensemble-inspired approach to embed two independent green-red watermarks using separate context windows and partitioning strategies. During generation, DualMark applies a tiered bias strategy, strongest to tokens in the intersection of both green lists while also biasing tokens unique to each list. Detection succeeds if either watermark yields a statistically significant signal. DualMark integrates seamlessly with existing watermarking schemes and incurs minimal overhead. Extensive experiments across various adversarial scenarios demonstrate that DualMark maintains text quality while substantially outperforming single-watermark baselines: it improves detection AUROC by over 11% under severe word-deletion attacks and doubles the true positive rate (TP@1%) against adaptive baselines under heavy paraphrasing, all while incurring only a 5% increase in generation latency.

papers.title: Network infrastructure construction and digital innovation resilience: Evidence from Broadband China policy
papers.authors: Jiang W., Jiang N., Yu D.
papers.abstract: We use data from 271 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2023 and treat the Broadband China policy as a quasi-natural experiment to examine how network infrastructure construction influences digital innovation resilience. The results indicate that network infrastructure construction raises digital innovation resilience. This conclusion remains valid after instrumental variable estimation and a series of robustness tests. This effect is particularly pronounced in cities characterized by high traditional infrastructure construction, low intellectual property protection, and strong government support for science and education. Mechanism analysis suggests that resilience is enhanced mainly through narrowing the digital divide and fostering innovation collaboration, while the mediating role of digital finance is not supported. This study adds to the literature on digital innovation resilience and offers policy insights for promoting network infrastructure construction in a sustainable way.

papers.title: MSSFN: Multi-stimulus stereo spatiotemporal fusion network with pattern disentanglement for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis
papers.authors: Zhang W., Jing P., Li X., Ji Y., Liu Y., Kung S.Y.
papers.abstract: Eye movements have been established as biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Current methods use diverse cognitive stimuli to elicit diagnostic responses, but face two challenges: the lack of 3D spatiotemporal modeling for comprehensive fusion and the entanglement of cognitive patterns within and across stimuli. To overcome these challenges, we propose the multi-stimulus stereo spatiotemporal fusion network (MSSFN) for AD diagnosis. The MSSFN contains two core modules: (1) stereo spatiotemporal embedding fuses binocular spatial fixation distributions, temporal scanpath dynamics, and stereo priors to establish unified 3D spatiotemporal eye movement modeling; (2) local-sensitive contrastive disentanglement implicitly extracts and decouples intrinsic cognitive patterns via a local-sensitive attention and a cognitive contrastive constraint to separate diagnostic cognitive patterns across stimulus paradigms. In addition, demographic-guided cognitive aggregation incorporates participant information as auxiliary covariates in the final decision. On a demographically matched, clinic-recruited cohort of 100 clinically diagnosed AD patients and 100 healthy controls (age: 72.12  ±  6.18 years), participants completed three stimulus paradigms: saccade, visual search, and visual attention. Under subject-wise 5-fold cross-validation, MSSFN demonstrates superior performance, achieving 0.87 accuracy, 0.87 AUC, 0.88 sensitivity, and 0.86 specificity, surpassing the strongest baseline MCGRL (0.81 accuracy) by 7.4%. Ablation studies further verify the contributions of the proposed modules. These results suggest that MSSFN enables efficient eye movement based AD screening as a complement to existing AD biomarkers, supporting future large-scale deployment.

papers.title: Robust social bot detection via multi-relational and noise-aware representation modeling
papers.authors: Liu F., Jiang B., Ma R.
papers.abstract: With the rapid proliferation of social platforms, bot-driven manipulation has become increasingly pervasive, underscoring the urgent need for robust social bot detection. Although recent work advances multi-relational and heterophily-aware modeling, many frameworks still fuse heterogeneous relations in a relation-agnostic way, amplifying structural noise and causing over-smoothing under heterophily or adversarial conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose BotMGTD, the first social bot detection framework to integrate target-conditioned multi-relational graph encoding with diffusion-based denoising. Specifically, BotMGTD constructs relation-specific subgraph embeddings and designates one dominant relation as the target to anchor message passing, while adaptively incorporating auxiliary relations via attention-based fusion. A latent diffusion denoiser, conditioned on the target representation, iteratively suppresses structural and feature perturbations in the latent space, improving stability on heterogeneous multi-relation graphs. Compared with the baselines, BotMGTD is consistently the most noise-robust, achieving the best performance under latent-space noise injection, edge perturbation, adversarial node infiltration, and cross-dataset transfer, with markedly smaller accuracy degradation than competing methods. The code is available at: https://github.com/FengLiuii/BotMGTD.

papers.title: DCFRec: Sequential recommendation via diffusion denoisingand context-aware frequency-domain analysis
papers.authors: Yang Y., Ju S., Zhao R., Li Y., Chen L.
papers.abstract: Sequential recommendationaims to accurately capture users’ dynamic preferences. However,existing models still face critical challenges in decoupling users’true preferences from interaction noise and effectively modeling thecomplex multi-scale periodic patterns in user behavior. To addressthese challenges, we propose Diffusion Denoising and Context-awareFrequency-domain analysis for Sequential Recommendation (DCFRec). Thismodel adopts a “denoising-analysis” architecture, integratingdiffusion denoising with time-domain and frequency-domain analysisthrough end-to-end joint optimization. Specifically, we devise areverse denoising network that combines bidirectional Mamba to capturelong-range ordered dependencies and a bidirectional self-attentionmechanism to capture global contextual correlations. This network aimsto generate a more robust representation of user behavior sequencesthrough signal reconstruction. The denoised sequence representation isthen fed into a parallel dual-analysis structure: a Fourier analysismodule that adaptively decouples and aggregates multi-scale periodicpatterns using a learnable frequency band attention mechanism, and atime-domain Transformer encoder that simultaneously models sequentialdependencies. The outputs from both modules are ultimately fused togenerate the final user preference representation. DCFRec is optimizedthrough joint training to enhance both its robustness andrecommendation accuracy. Experiments on five real-world datasetsdemonstrate that DCFRec significantly outperforms state-of-the-artmethods across various recommendation metrics, with an averageimprovement of 6.8% on HR@20 and 7.4% on NDCG@20, validating itseffectiveness in capturing diverse user preferences and achievingrobust learning. papers.title: Fine-grained dynamic graph learning for irregular multivariate time series
papers.authors: Ji J., Hou C., Cao Y., Ma Y., Yan J.
papers.abstract: Irregular Multivariate Time Series (IMTS) are prevalent in many real-world applications but pose significant challenges for representation learning because of missing values, unequal sequence lengths, and asynchronous sampling. Recent methods attempt to alleviate these challenges through techniques such as interpolation, continuous-time modeling, attention mechanisms, and graph learning. However, these methods frequently fail to capture the evolving temporal dependencies and dynamic interactions among variables, leading to suboptimal performance in high sparsity and irregularity. To address these challenges, we propose FgDGL, a novel Fine-grained Dynamic Graph Learning framework. FgDGL proposes a multi-lag partial correlation initialization mechanism to initialize graph structures, thereby providing a causally grounded, lag-aware graph prior. This mechanism captures decaying autocorrelation dependencies and cross-variable conditional interactions with irregular observation intervals. Moreover, FgDGL further develops a fine-grained incremental adjacency matrix update scheme guided by a semantic memory, thereby acting as a temporal regularizer for dynamic graph evolution. This scheme aligns the evolving adjacency matrix with temporally consistent structures and reduces spurious correlations caused by missing values, without requiring global updates. Finally, the latent representations at the last observed time step are fused with optional static covariates, enabling robust classification under unequal sequence lengths. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that FgDGL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in IMTS classification, achieving improvements of up to 1.4% AUROC and 2.6% AUPRC improvements over the best baselines.

papers.title: Hierarchical dynamic pattern analysis and adaptive fusion of multimodal physiological signals for emotion recognition
papers.authors: Xu Z., Chen N., Li G., Tian Y., Zhu H., Zhu Z.
papers.abstract: AbstractThe inherent dynamic characteristics that exist in the temporal and spatial domains of different physiological signals, as well as in cross-modal collaborative relationships among them, are highly related to emotional states. However, these properties are overlooked in the previously proposed multimodal emotion recognition models. To address this limitation, a new fusion model that effectively combines the above emotion-related neuroscience prior knowledge is proposed. First, a temporal progressive pattern extraction strategy is introduced by segmenting signals into multiple phases, extracting differential entropy features from each phase, and adopting the modified depthwise separable convolution to capture the temporal progressive pattern across phases. Second, a spatial asymmetric coupling pattern extraction method based on the multi-layer graph attention network is designed to capture multi-scale spatial asymmetric coupling features. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy based on the cross-modal Transformer is developed to adaptively fuse emotion-related components in modality-consistent information and those in modality-specific information. Experimental results on DEAP, DREAMER, and PhyMER indicate that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an accuracy improvement of 0.99%-14.46% (0.82%-6.77%) and F1 score improvement of 0.48%-16.23% (0.17%-7.41%) under subject-dependent (subject-independent) scenarios, in binary and four-class classification tasks with equivalent or even smaller computational complexity. Moreover, all the key modules in the above-designed methods contribute to the performance enhancement. Our findings indicate that extracting the dynamic patterns existing in the temporal and spatial domains of each physiological signal, and those reflected in the cross-modal collaborative relationships, enhances the emotion representation ability and interpretability of the proposed model.

papers.title: Toward better pragmatic tagging of peer review: Enhancing benchmark datasets via human-in-the-loop multi-agent collaboration
papers.authors: He G., Su T., Zhang M., Yuan J., Jiang Z., Ma L., Xiao B., Zhu X.
papers.abstract: Pragmatic tagging datasets for peer review, i.e., sentence-level functional annotations, are essential for assessing review quality and developing intelligent review systems. However, existing benchmark datasets often suffer from annotation inconsistencies and limited coverage. To address these issues, we propose a Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework (HMCF) for verifying, correcting, and expanding pragmatic annotation datasets. HMCF first leverages a large language model (LLM), prompted by annotation guidelines, serving as a large agent that validates human annotations and suggests corrections. Annotations where the human and large agent agree constitute the gold data, which is then used to fine-tune a smaller pretrained language model (PLM) as a small agent. The small agent helps resolve disagreements between human and large agent annotations, while unresolved cases are adjudicated by additional experts. Experiments show that HMCF reduces human effort, improves annotation consistency, and reveals the categories most susceptible to annotation errors. Moreover, the small agent enables large-scale annotation of unlabeled peer reviews, yielding richer, high-quality resources. Collectively, HMCF demonstrates both theoretical significance and practical value in advancing pragmatic tagging of peer review. The corrected and expanded dataset is publicly available athttps://huggingface.co/datasets/andy8/HMCF. The code is publicly available athttps://github.com/ECNU-Text-Computing/HMCF.

papers.title: DataFactory: Collaborative multi-agent framework for advanced table question answering
papers.authors: Wang T., Jin C., Chen Y., Deng H., Kuang X., Zhao G.
papers.abstract: Table Question Answering (TableQA) enables natural language interaction with structured tabular data. However, existing large language model (LLM) approaches face critical limitations: context length constraints that restrict data handling capabilities, hallucination issues that compromise answer reliability, and single-agent architectures that struggle with complex reasoning scenarios involving semantic relationships and multi-hop logic. This paper introduces DataFactory, a multi-agent framework that addresses these limitations through specialized team coordination and automated knowledge transformation. The framework comprises a Data Leader employing the ReAct paradigm for reasoning orchestration, together with dedicated Database and Knowledge Graph teams, enabling the systematic decomposition of complex queries into structured and relational reasoning tasks. We formalize automated data-to-knowledge graph transformation via the mapping function (Formula presented), and implement natural language-based consultation that—unlike fixed workflow multi-agent systems—enables flexible inter-agent deliberation and adaptive planning to improve coordination robustness; we also apply context engineering strategies that integrate historical patterns and domain knowledge to reduce hallucinations and improve query accuracy. Across TabFact, WikiTableQuestions, and FeTaQA, using eight LLMs from five providers, results show consistent gains. Our approach improves accuracy by 20.2% (TabFact) and 23.9% (WikiTQ) over baselines, with significant effects (Cohen’s d>1). Team coordination also outperforms single-team variants (+5.5% TabFact, +14.4% WikiTQ, +17.1% FeTaQA ROUGE-2). The framework offers design guidelines for multi-agent collaboration and a practical platform for enterprise data analysis through integrated structured querying and graph-based knowledge representation.

papers.title: Reasoning-guided structured planning and search in large language models
papers.authors: Shen Y., Shi W.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often fail on time-sensitive queries without external search. We present R-Search, a single-LLM framework that produces a structured trace: <think> reasoning, a natural-language directed acyclic graph (NL-DAG) <search>, executed results <result>, and a final <answer>. The model is trained with reinforcement fine-tuning (ReFT) using a composite reward for answer accuracy, DAG validity, and format compliance. We construct a training set of 1000 multi-hop Q&A pairs from recent news and academic abstracts. On FinSearchBench-24, R-Search attains 78.13% with 1535 tokens/answer and 8.58 s latency, outperforming multi-agent and single-LLM baselines and cutting tokens and latency by approximately 70% and 50% versus FinSearch. On SearchExpertBench-25, it reaches 73.0% with comparable efficiency. Across seven QA datasets, it averages 41.87% EM. These results indicate that explicit NL-DAG planning within a single LLM narrows the plan-execution gap and improves both effectiveness and efficiency for search-augmented generation.

papers.title: Fuzzy neighborhood rough set-based attribute reduction over temporal information systems with application to clinical efficacy evaluation
papers.authors: Chang X., Sun B., Liu X., Ye J., Chu X.
papers.abstract: Efficacy evaluation is an important topic in medical management. In unlabeled, multi-time point clinical follow-up data characterized by high dimensionality, temporal imbalance, attribute heterogeneity, and missing values, performing effective attribute reduction remains a key challenge. Assessing individual state changes between adjacent time points is also challenging. To address these issues, this study proposes a framework for unsupervised attribute reduction and dynamic trend discrimination in temporal information systems. First, a temporal information system is constructed to handle data with imbalanced, incomplete, and heterogeneous attributes. Second, based on Gaussian-kernel fuzzy relations and a multi-β neighborhood coverage approximation, a set of unsupervised quality metrics and a joint optimization objective Q is developed. The objective Q serves as a unified criterion driving both attribute reduction and learning. It enables flexible trade-offs among coverage, consistency, stability, and robustness to obtain more discriminative and interpretable attributes. Next, we employ a state-space model to smooth latent health state estimates. Further, we introduce false discovery rate (FDR) control to adaptively determine classification thresholds. We also incorporate an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) evidence-accumulation mechanism to capture gradual trends. The proposed method outperforms nine comparative methods, further demonstrating its scientific validity and feasibility. Additionally, sensitivity analyses and ablation experiments confirm its robustness and generalizability. papers.title: Explicit geometric relationships under limited spatial reference points guide 3D visual grounding
papers.authors: Wang Z., Li C., Ma J., Feng Z., Wang P., Wang X., Xiao L.
papers.abstract: Three-Dimensional Visual Grounding (3DVG) aims to locate objects in 3D scenes based on natural language queries. Existing methods typically rely on absolute position encoding of global objects to model spatial relationships for target localization. However, this often results in inadequate spatial understanding and redundant or invalid encoding. To address these limitations, we propose the Relative K-object Fusion Perception 3D Visual Grounding (3DRelKG) framework. By dynamically sampling a limited number of scene reference points, our approach enhances the modeling of spatial relationships for localization targets by learning only the positional and relative spherical geometric features of these reference points with respect to scene objects. Additionally, we introduce a heterogeneous feature fusion module, whose core is an information interaction mechanism based on the similarity matrix of heterogeneous features. This approach naturally avoids the problem of unreliable attention interaction weights that arise from directly calculating the similarity between heterogeneous features. Experiments on ScanRefer, SR3D, and NR3D demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art models, improving accuracy by 2.3%, 4.3%, and 2.1%, respectively, and increasing inference speed by 43.8%.

papers.title: Multimodal fake news video explanation: Dataset, model and evaluation
papers.authors: Chen L., Qian Z., Li P., Zhu Q.
papers.abstract: AbstractWhile social media platforms facilitate information access, fake news videos pose serious societal risks. Most detection methods treat fake news as a binary classification problem, ignoring the unique deceptive patterns of each fake item. To address this, we introduce the Fake News Video Explanation (FNVE) task, which generates natural language explanations for fake news videos. To support this, we develop FakeVE, a new dataset comprising 2672 fake news video posts, which provides explicit explanations for four real-world deceptive aspects of fake news videos. Furthermore, we propose a Multimodal Relation Graph Transformer (MRGT) model that explicitly models intra- and inter-modal inconsistencies via graph reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MRGT achieves state-of-the-art performance on FakeVE, outperforming strong baselines including recent Multimodal Large Language Models by up to +1.36 in BLEU-4 and +8.80 in ROUGE-L. Our work provides the first systematic benchmark for generating explanations for false news video, and highlights the importance of specialized architectures for this task. We release our code and dataset at https://github.com/Lieberk/FakeVE.

papers.title: ALC-DRKG: an active learning-based framework for dynamic knowledge graph construction for drug repositioning
papers.authors: Liu S., Xu H., Wang X., Zan P., He S., Bo X.
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graph (KG) technology plays a key role in drug repurposing. Current KGs for drug repurposing are predominantly constructed from limited static databases, commonly exhibiting data sparsity issues. Dynamic KG construction techniques can reduce this issue by extracting triples from biomedical literature. However, its incremental strategy of direct integration may result in redundancy of information, leading to a decrease in downstream task model prediction accuracy. Considering this, this paper defines the dynamic KG construction process as an active selection problem involving information-rich triples and introduces active learning (AL) to address it. It proposes the Active Learning Collection for Drug Repositioning Knowledge Graph (ALC-DRKG) framework. We propose two AL algorithms: entity clustering combined with uncertainty (EC-U) and power law distribution combined with uncertainty (PL-U). EC-U enhances data balance by clustering entities to capture latent relationships between them. PL-U captures global critical association information based on the scale-free properties of biomedical networks. We use two drug repositioning knowledge graph (DRKG) datasets, HetioNet (2250,197 triples) and Multiscale Interactome Network (MSI) (478,728 triples), to validate ALC-DRKG. Experiments show that proposed algorithms significantly outperform traditional algorithms, with an average improvement of 28.4%. Especially on the MSI dataset, ours achieves over 80% of full-dataset performance using 25% of the data, while surpassing full-dataset performance in the Hits@1 metric. Meanwhile, we conduct an interpretable analysis of the proposed algorithms' performance advantages based on network theory. The study provides an efficient way to optimize the construction of dynamic DRKGs. The code and data are available at https://github.com/hiL-hiL/ALC-DRKG.

papers.title: Empowering open-domain LLMs for legal document correction via legal knowledge integration and decoding constraints
papers.authors: Zhang K., Yu W., Sun Z., Qin W., Xu J., Wen J.R.
papers.abstract: Legal document correction is essential for ensuring the accuracy and validity of legal texts. While open-domain large language models (LLMs) perform well on general text correction, they often make substantive errors in legal contexts due to limited domain knowledge. Fine-tuning can inject legal knowledge but is computationally costly and may introduce over-correction and mechanical errors. To address these challenges, we propose Legal Document Correction (LDC), a lightweight two-stage framework that enables open-domain LLMs to correct legal documents with high accuracy using only 1,000 training samples. LDC first constructs a legal knowledge base from formal legal expressions and statutory articles. In Stage 1, it applies retrieval-augmented fine-tuning to mitigate substantive legal errors. In Stage 2, it detects over-correction and applies constrained decoding to preserve legal elements while fixing mechanical issues. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and data efficiency of LDC. On CAIL, LDC improves F<inf>0.5</inf> from 13.89 to 52.12 and reduces false-positive edits from 800 to 49; on Tailing, it improves F<inf>0.5</inf> from 40.92 to 74.77 and reduces false-positive edits from 1119 to 167. With only 100 training examples, LDC achieves up to 763% and 269% improvements in F<inf>0.5</inf> on CAIL and Tailing, respectively.

papers.title: From graphs to tokens: Substructure-aware molecular representation for large language models
papers.authors: Wang R., Xing Z., Liu X., Yang M., He C., Shen Y.
papers.abstract: AbstractEnabling large language models (LLMs) to process graph-structured data holds significant potential for advancing molecular research, especially in tasks related to molecular structure analysis and understanding. However, a key challenge remains in effectively tokenizing molecular graphs to align with the capabilities of LLMs. To bridge the gap, this paper proposes SubStructure-aware Tokenization (S2Token) that fragments molecules into chemically meaningful, reusable substructures. The key idea is to generate semantically enriched substructure token embeddings and represent the complex relationships between tokens in the LLM embedding space, allowing LLMs to learn and generalize chemical patterns effectively. To achieve this, S2Token begins by decomposing molecular graphs based on frequency and functionality to build a vocabulary. Then, we establish a dual-view token embedding method that jointly encodes fine-grained structural and functional attributes of molecular substructures. Furthermore, we propose an efficient token alignment strategy to associate the dependencies between non-sequential substructures with the LLM token embedding space. In this way, our method activates the LLMs’ generalization ability to unseen molecular graphs. To evaluate this, we curate four task-specific molecular datasets designed to investigate generalization. Extensive experiments on three standard benchmarks and four curated datasets demonstrate that S2Token consistently yields substantial performance improvements. On the molecular caption benchmark, S2Token achieves a 12.6% average performance gain across six metrics, outperforming the best LLM-based method. For forward reaction and retrosynthesis tasks, it enhances fingerprint similarity for synthesized molecules by 6.6% and 8.6%, respectively. Moreover, S2Token shows advantages on four generalist evaluation tasks, including 9.7% and 3.0% reductions in MAE on the molecular property prediction task, compared to graph- and node-centric tokenization methods. papers.title: SCGRN: Spatiotemporal causal graph reasoning network for regional economic development modeling
papers.authors: Zhou L., Wang M., Chen Q., Han H.
papers.abstract: High-quality economic development calls for data-driven, interpretable modeling to support regional policy decisions. However, existing forecasting methods struggle with causal reasoning and spatiotemporal integration. Traditional econometric models capture structural relationships but often miss complex nonlinear patterns, while recent machine learning models (e.g., deep neural networks) achieve accuracy at the cost of interpretability. In particular, current spatiotemporal graph neural networks (ST-GNNs) assume fixed or learned correlations but lack explicit causal modeling and struggle to jointly capture spatial spillovers and temporal dynamics. To address these gaps, we propose a Spatiotemporal Causal Graph Reasoning Network (SCGRN) that integrates causal discovery, spatial graph learning, temporal sequence modeling, and counterfactual policy simulation. SCGRN first uncovers a directed acyclic causal graph of key economic factors, then embeds regions in a spatial graph neural network, and finally models temporal dynamics with recurrent units-all guided by the causal graph. Experiments on a 21-year panel dataset covering 31 Chinese provincial-level regions (651 province-year observations) demonstrate a 12.3% reduction in RMSE over state-of-the-art baselines, and SCGRN recovers economically plausible directed relations consistent with prior evidence. Moreover, SCGRN supports policy scenario analysis: by simulating interventions, it generates interpretable counterfactual outcomes for decision-makers. This work provides a novel interpretable AI approach for regional economic development modeling, with practical potential for evidence-based policy and resource allocation.

papers.title: A novel K-shell-based feature for detecting influential nodes in directed complex networks: Addressing resolution and core-like groups problems
papers.authors: Esfandiari S., Fakhrahmad M.
papers.abstract: The identification of influential nodes plays a crucial role in understanding the dynamics of complex networks. However, most existing methods, particularly when applied to directed networks, still suffer from limited resolution and accuracy. To address these issues, we propose three variants of the k-shell method specifically designed for directed networks and introduce a hybrid approach that integrates k-shell with degree centrality. This combination resolves the challenges of low resolution and the core-like group problem in both directed and undirected networks. To support this, we provide a mathematical formulation. Furthermore, to validate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct extensive experiments using the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) model on 27 real-world networks, including 19 undirected and 8 directed networks, and compare the results against 27 benchmark methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves accuracy by 57.8% over Balanced Iterative Influence (BII) and 53.5% over Return Random Walk Gravity (RRWG), while maintaining linear time complexity and higher precision. These findings indicate that the proposed method is both scalable and robust, offering a more reliable framework for analyzing influence in complex directed networks.

papers.title: Refine and reflect: Explainable stock predictions with large language models
papers.authors: Lin J., Gao Z., Tang X.
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting stock movements from investor-generated text is challenging due to noisy discourse and the need for interpretable reasoning. We propose a novel explainable prediction framework that integrates sentiment modeling, event extraction, a dual-stage reflection mechanism, and reinforcement learning optimization. Using 194,304 investor comments from East Money forums (covering A-share firms, 2022–2024), the framework constructs sentiment indices and structured events to guide a large language model in generating both forecasts and causal explanations. A reflection module enables the model to identify and correct reasoning errors, and fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) balances accuracy with interpretability. Experiments on an independent test set of 70,000 comments show that our method improves prediction accuracy to 54.5% (a 3.7% gain over the base model) and enhances explanation quality by over 20%. These results demonstrate a scalable path toward transparent and trustworthy financial AI.

papers.title: Opinion maximization on social trust networks considering local and global information
papers.authors: Yu L., Wang Y., Yang F., Fu D., Shi F., Yao C.
papers.abstract: Opinion maximization extends traditional influence maximization by aiming to maximize the spread of desired opinions rather than merely the number of influenced nodes. In this paper, we propose a continuous opinion dynamics model for Social Trust Networks (STNs), incorporating both global public information and local consensus information into opinion updates. We prove that the formulated optimization problem is NP-hard, and its objective function is non-monotone and non-submodular. To address this challenge, we develop a two-stage seed selection algorithm (TSSA) that first filters potential seeds using a heuristic rule and then applies a Greedy strategy to determine the final seed set. Experiments conducted on four real-world social network datasets illustrate that TSSA consistently outperforms several baseline algorithms, and maintains stable performance across different network structures. Comparison with a greedy algorithm further confirms that TSSA provides substantial computational advantages while retaining a high level of solution quality. Specifically, TSSA achieves a reduction in computation time by approximately one to three orders of magnitude, while its opinion maximization results remain very close to those of Greedy, with only a 0.13 % to 3.98 % decline in the final objective value. Additional simulation studies reveal that both global public information and the opinion interaction threshold play a significant role in enhancing the performance of opinion maximization.

papers.title: Dual-view fusion of structure and behavior: A robust learning item recommendation framework against interest drift and cold-start
papers.authors: Luo N., Zhao Y., Zhang J., Ni Y.
papers.abstract: Accurately modeling learners’ evolving interests and knowledge structures remains a key challenge in online learning-item recommendation, especially in cold-start and interest-drift scenarios. This paper proposes a dual-view preference recommendation framework, called DVPRec, which jointly captures learners’ long-term knowledge preferences and short-term behavioral dynamics. Specifically, a graph-based structural view models latent knowledge dependencies and group-level learning patterns through subgraph partitioning, structural denoising, and layer-attentive graph convolution. Meanwhile, a sequential behavioral view uses Transformer-based modeling to track short-term, goal-driven interest shifts. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically combines the two views to balance long-term stability and short-term responsiveness in recommendation decisions. Extensive experiments are conducted on two large-scale real-world educational datasets: EdNet-KT1 and Assistments2017 (filtered), which contain tens of thousands of learners, thousands of items, and millions of interactions, respectively. Compared with state-of-the-art graph-based and sequential baseline models, DVPRec consistently achieves better performance. On EdNet-KT1, DVPRec improves Recall@10, NDCG@10, and MRR by 3.6 %, 3.7 %, and 3.4 %, respectively. On the sparser Assistments2017 dataset, the improvements are more notable, with Recall@10 and MRR increasing by 6.8 % and 6.2 %. Ablation studies further show that both structural denoising and dynamic interest fusion are critical to these improvements. These findings confirm that jointly modeling structural regularities from interaction graphs and short-term behavioral dynamics provides a robust recommendation approach. This approach effectively balances long-term pattern consistency with short-term adaptability in the context of sparse and evolving interaction data.

papers.title: Beyond textual knowledge: Leveraging multimodal knowledge bases for enhancing vision-and-language navigation
papers.authors: Yang D., Yu Y., Wang L.
papers.abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to navigate through complex unseen environments based on natural language instructions. However, existing methods often struggle to effectively capture key semantic cues and accurately align them with visual observations. To address this limitation, we propose Beyond Textual Knowledge (BTK), a VLN framework that synergistically integrates environment-specific textual knowledge with generative image knowledge bases. BTK employs Qwen3-4B to extract goal-related phrases and utilizes Flux-Schnell to construct two large-scale image knowledge bases: R2R_GP and REVERIE_GP. Additionally, we leverage BLIP-2 to construct a large-scale textual knowledge base derived from panoramic views, providing environment-specific semantic cues. These multimodal knowledge bases are effectively integrated via the Goal-Aware Augmentor and Knowledge Augmentor, significantly enhancing semantic grounding and cross-modal alignment. Extensive experiments on the R2R dataset with 7189 trajectories and the REVERIE dataset with 21,702 instructions demonstrate that BTK significantly outperforms existing baselines. On the test unseen splits of R2R and REVERIE, SR increased by 5% and 2.07% respectively, and SPL increased by 4% and 3.69% respectively. papers.title: DRUM: Distributionally robust optimization for LLM-based user model in interactive recommendation
papers.authors: Liu H., Quan Y., Wang Z., Ma H., Wu X.
papers.abstract: Interactive Recommender Systems (IRSs) learn the dynamic changes in user interests through multi-step interactions. Considering training costs, most Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based IRSs are developed offline. These systems leverage user log data to train a user model, which provides feedback for training the RL agent. However, existing approaches primarily use neural networks to construct user models, which struggle to achieve high-quality modeling in the face of data sparsity. To address this issue, we utilize Large Language Models (LLMs) with rich world knowledge as the user model in IRSs. Meanwhile, recognizing that LLMs may introduce distribution shifts between generated and real user feedback due to biases in their pretraining corpora, we introduce Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) and propose a method called Distributionally Robust Optimization for LLM-based User Model (DRUM) in Interactive Recommendation. Specifically, we first align LLMs with recommendation tasks through instruction fine-tuning to serve as the user model in IRSs. Then, we construct an exposure simulator using a mixture of multiple recommendation models to generate an exposure distribution that can be used as the nominal distribution for DRO. Finally, we incorporate the obtained exposure distribution and add penalty prompts to the original prompt template to further fine-tune the LLM-based user model, mitigating the impact of biases in the pretraining corpora. Experimental results demonstrate that DRUM improves recommendation performance and enhances model robustness in data-sparse scenarios, with cumulative reward improvements of 24.06%, 38.27%, and 4.33% and interaction length improvements of 1.11%, 1.08%, and 1.54% on three datasets, respectively.

papers.title: Dynamic alignment of visual and language semantics for referring video object segmentation
papers.authors: Cao Y., Wang Y., Sun L., Zou X., Ma Y.
papers.abstract: Referring Video Object Segmentation (RVOS) aims to segment objects in videos based on language expressions. In this task, existing methods often face challenges due to semantic misalignment between language and visual modalities. To address this, this paper categorizes semantic misalignment into word-level, sentence-level, and cognitive-level issues. For these issues, we propose the Dynamic Alignment of Visual and Language Semantics (DAVLS) framework. In DAVLS, to address word-level semantic misalignment, we design the Word-level Semantic Dynamic Alignment (WSDA) to maximize the alignment of word-level semantics with appropriate visual features by embedding them into frame-level visual features and enabling cross-modal fusion visually. Based on accurate sentence-level object semantics generated by the textual adapter (TA), we propose the Sentence-level Semantic Dynamic Alignment (SSDA) to address sentence-level misalignment by aligning these semantics with the visual object state of the video clip. Due to the intrinsic linkage between WSDA and SSDA, they are integrated into a unified module, named SDA. Moreover, to mitigate the cognitive-level misalignment between humans and the segmentation model in understanding the semantics of referring objects, we introduce Semantic Augmentation (SA) to enhance the model’s comprehension of object semantics by expanding linguistic expressions. Simulation results on Ref-YouTube-VOS (3,978 videos), Ref-DAVIS17 (90 videos), A2D-Sentences (3,782 videos), and JHMDB-Sentences (928 videos) demonstrate the competitive performance of DAVLS, achieving a 0.9% improvement in (Formula presented) on Ref-YouTube-VOS and a 1.0% increase in Overall IoU on A2D-Sentences. Moreover, a statistically significant result ((Formula presented) ), validated by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, confirms the reliability of the performance gains.

papers.title: A framework for hallucination mitigation in domain-specialized large language models with application to aviation maintenance decision support
papers.authors: Lu X., Su X., Feng J., Zeng K., Zhang S., Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: AbstractHallucination in large language models (LLMs) poses significant risks when applied to safety-critical domains such as aviation maintenance. To address this challenge, this study proposes HALC (Hallucination-Aware LLM for Critical Scenarios), a reliability-centered reasoning framework designed to ensure factual consistency through evidence-grounded, stepwise verification and uncertainty-aware control in domain-specialized LLMs. HALC establishes a closed-loop reliability architecture integrating two complementary mechanisms: a semantic-entropy-based hallucination detection mechanism that quantifies step-level uncertainty to identify potential inconsistencies, and a multi-source retrieval-augmented verification chain that cross-validates generated reasoning steps against maintenance records and technical manuals with traceable citations. Experiments conducted on 2443 real-world maintenance records, evaluated across 30 benchmark retrieval cases and a validated 199-sample test subset, demonstrate that HALC effectively mitigates hallucinations, achieving a substantial (>85 %) reduction in unsafe acceptance risk, operationalized as false positive acceptance under fixed high-safety (low-FPR) constraints, and a ∼20 % improvement in factual reliability compared to domain-tuned baselines. The proposed framework contributes to advancing trustworthy and explainable LLM reasoning, providing a scalable pathway for reliable deployment of LLMs in safety-critical industrial applications such as intelligent maintenance and fault diagnosis.

papers.title: Learning to rank critical road segments via heterogeneous graphs with origin-destination flow integration
papers.authors: Xu M., Xiang J., Xie Z., Meng X.
papers.abstract: Existing learning-to-rank methods for road networks often fail to incorporate origin-destination (OD) flows and route information, limiting their ability to model long-range spatial dependencies. To address this gap, we propose HetGL2R, a heterogeneous graph learning framework for ranking road-segment importance. HetGL2R builds a tripartite graph that unifies OD flows, routes, and network topology, and further introduces attribute-guided graphs that elevate node attributes into explicit nodes to model functional similarity. A heterogeneous joint random walk algorithm (HetGWalk) jointly samples both graph types to generate context-rich node sequences. These sequences are encoded using a Transformer to learn embeddings that capture long-range structural dependencies induced by OD flows and route configurations, as well as functional associations derived from attribute similarity. Finally, a listwise ranking strategy with a KL-divergence loss evaluates and ranks segment importance. Experiments on three SUMO-generated simulated networks of different scales show that, against state-of-the-art methods, HetGL2R achieves average improvements of approximately 7.52%, 4.40% and 3.57% in ranking performance.

papers.title: AI-driven remanufacturing supply chains: Greening and intelligence diffusion
papers.authors: Zhu J., Yang L., Zhou W.
papers.abstract: AbstractArtificial intelligence (AI) based training recycled data was applied in remanufacturing to minimize the screening and inspection misses. We focus on the diffusion of green practices and intelligent technology when AI is applied to remanufacturing supply chains and how to control. A remanufacturing supply chain network is constructed based on epidemic models with a three-stage game, where an AI provider activates, then firms produce, and consumers purchase. This model captures the firms’ learning and consumers’ imitation, and reveals a seesaw effect between the self-driven power from AI and the out-driven power from the AI provider. We show that appropriately leveraging influential “big customers” with high hyperdegree and configuring network connectivity can promote greening and intelligence diffusion. Interestingly, contrary to traditional wisdom, higher data efficiency and accuracy of AI do not always accelerate diffusion, highlighting the potential mismatch between technological performance and adoption. Based on 16 parameter experiments, each involving over 2000 data instances with 100 replicates, simulations indicate that incomplete diffusion is general. However, adjusting these factors increase the greening and intelligence diffusion level to up to 94.73% and 81.50%, while inspection misses are reduced by 38.11% compared to the baseline. These results imply that more firms are induced to remanufacture and adopt AI-enabled inspection, so as to improve operational efficiency and reduce waste. Furthermore, neither the remanufacturer nor the third-party technical vendor is universally dominant as an AI provider, as their motivations to activate AI adoption vary across industry contexts. Overall, we indicate that promoting green practices and smart technologies depends on the integration of network structure, product design, and technical attributes, rather than relying solely on technical performance or provider identity.

papers.title: Integrating managerial and investor textual data for financial distress prediction: A framework combining multi-source financial information fusion network with LLM
papers.authors: Qiu J., Cui S., Fan W., Gao R.
papers.abstract: While prior financial distress prediction (FDP) studies have increasingly incorporated multi-source data, existing approaches rarely integrate financial indicators with fine-grained narrative signals in a unified framework. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel FDP framework that integrates simultaneously financial ratios, Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), and investor comments from social media. We first propose an LLM-BERT based triplet extraction approach to capture aspect-level semantic and sentiment information from MD&A texts. Second, we utilize FinBERT to extract sentiment features from investor comments. These textual features are then combined with financial ratios and integrated into a Multi-source Financial Information Fusion Network (MFIFN), trained with focal loss to mitigate class imbalance. Based on the dataset of 24,429 firm-year samples from Chinese listed companies between 2014 and 2023 (including both distressed and non-distressed firms), experimental results demonstrate that incorporating social media and MD&A features provides incremental predictive values on top of financial ratios. In particular, the proposed MFIFN model achieves an AUC of 0.9541. Furthermore, the LLM-BERT based triplet extraction method improves feature quality, delivering consistent performance gains across compared with traditional textual feature extraction methods. These findings suggest that integrating financial indicators with fine-grained narrative signals can enhance early warning systems, providing stakeholders with more timely and comprehensive risk assessment tools.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware memory-enhanced cross-window dependency learning for robust multivariate time series anomaly detection
papers.authors: Xue B., Gao X., Diao X., Yu H., Li Y., Chen T., Xu H., Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Existing time series anomaly detection methods typically rely on fixed-length sliding windows for feature extraction, which constrains their ability to capture long-range dependencies and global temporal dynamics. Moreover, real-world data are often contaminated with anomalies, and the assumption of clean training data may lead to overfitting.While memory-based approaches aim to model normal patterns under such contamination, their fixed-dimensional representations struggle to capture the complexity and variability of normal dynamics and often ignore the intrinsic uncertainty in the normal pattern distribution, ultimately undermining detection accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes an Uncertainty-aware Memory-Enhanced Cross-Window Dependency Learning for robust multivariate time series anomaly detection (UMECD). A global-window dual positional encoding mechanism is proposed, where positional memory vectors store cross-window context and supervised regression of positional labels enables explicit learning of long-term dependencies and local dynamics. By jointly reconstructing features with integrated global and local positional information, the model enhances temporal representation and generalization. Furthermore, a Bayesian memory module probabilistically models normal patterns through Gaussian distributions and reparameterized sampling, effectively suppressing noise and improving adaptability to input variations. The method is evaluated against 23 state-of-the-art multivariate time series anomaly detection approaches on five real-world datasets using three evaluation metrics.It achieves the best overall average performance, with five best and two second-best results. Compared to the top-performing baseline, the average performance across all datasets and metrics improves by over 4.97%. Moreover, it obtains the lowest average rank across all metrics, confirming its superior effectiveness and robustness.

papers.title: Causal continual unlearning with disentangled anomaly representations for private industrial vision
papers.authors: Iqbal S., Zhong X., Khan M.A., Wu Z., Almujally N.A., Liu W., Hussain A.
papers.abstract: Continual Learning and Private Unlearning (CLPU) in industrial anomaly detection (IAD) demands lifelong adaptation to new product-defect pairs while enabling GDPR-compliant erasure of proprietary client data. Existing methods fail to reconcile three critical limitations: (i) disentanglement gap, inability to share universal anomaly primitives while isolating IP-sensitive semantics; (ii) causal leakage, unmodeled transitive privacy violations in multi-stage inspection pipelines; and (iii) memory inefficiency, prohibitive storage costs for high-resolution vision. We redefine unlearning not as parameter deletion, but as structured information control: a theoretically grounded process that selectively removes sensitive knowledge while preserving transferable representations. We introduce Causal Disentangled Industrial Unlearning (CaDIU), which establishes (1) privacy-preserving disentanglement via causally factorized latent spaces, (2) system-level causal indistinguishability through Defect Propagation Graphs with ancestral restoration, and (3) information-theoretic memory bounds enabling exact unlearning with (Formula presented) storage. Evaluated on four industrial benchmarks, VisA, MVTec-AD, Real-IAD, and BTAD, CaDIU achieves state-of-the-art performance: Anomaly Primitive Fidelity  ≥  0.96, IP Reconstruction Error  ≤  0.12, Causal Leakage Score  ≤  0.03, and Memory Efficiency Ratio = 0.08. Our framework is the first to enable efficient, private, and certifiable lifelong industrial vision, providing a foundation for GDPR-compliant, edge-deployable AI in multi-client manufacturing environments.

papers.title: Handling unseen entities with dual-level interaction dynamics in temporal knowledge graphs
papers.authors: Tian X., Zhang X., Du X., Lu T.
papers.abstract: Inductive reasoning on Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) aims to predict missing links with unseen entities, a practical yet under-explored task. Existing approaches relying on trained entity representations struggle to generalize to new entities. To address this challenge, we propose DIST (Dual-level Interaction in both Structural and Temporal dimensions), a relation-driven framework that captures rich relational patterns. Instead of relying on explicit entity information, it identifies multiple types of relational patterns from topological and chronological perspectives. The framework models dual-level interactions: (1) a relation-level Relational Pattern Encoder that encodes semantic representations for relations from diverse relational patterns, and (2) an entity-level Query-specific Temporal Reasoner that integrates these relation representations with fine-grained, query-specific context in TKGs. DIST shows competitive performance in transductive settings while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods in inductive scenarios. On ICEWS18-ind (inductive), DIST achieves average gains of 8.07% in MRR and 10.76% in Hits@1 over state-of-the-art inductive methods, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities. papers.title: Multi-view co-clustering with dynamic feature-level clustering candidates
papers.authors: Zhu W., Yan W.Q., Zhou Q.
papers.abstract: Multi-view co-clustering aims to simultaneously cluster instances and features by exploiting complementary information from multiple data perspectives. Existing approaches typically adopt a single, fixed clustering configuration along the feature dimension for each view, which may restrict the quality of learned consensus representations. To address this limitation, we propose a novel information-theoretic framework termed Dispersion in Clustering (DiC), which explicitly incorporates dynamic feature-level clustering candidates into multi-view co-clustering. The DiC framework consists of two core modules: Internal-view Candidates Exploitation (ICE) and Inter-view Consensus Clustering (ICC). In the ICE module, multiple feature-level clustering candidates are generated for each view, and their contributions are adaptively weighted through entropy minimization to reduce redundancy. In the ICC module, these candidates are integrated across views using learnable view weights regulated by entropy maximization, enabling balanced and robust consensus instance-level clustering. By jointly optimizing candidate-level and view-level weights, DiC effectively explores diverse feature-level structures without requiring prior specification of a single clustering configuration. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first multi-view co-clustering approach that involves dynamic clustering along the feature dimension. Experimental results on seven benchmark datasets, including Dermatology, ORL, ALOI, Caltech20, NUS-WIDE, HW Digits, and CIFAR-10, with sample sizes ranging from 366 to 60,000 instances and from 2 to 7 views, show that DiC outperforms state-of-the-art co-clustering algorithms, achieving an average improvement of 3.68% in ACC, 2.53% in NMI, and 3.73% in Purity, thereby highlighting the effectiveness of dynamic feature-level clustering candidates in enhancing multi-view co-clustering performance.

papers.title: Uncovering the formation dynamics of technology convergence: A multi-dimensional BTERGM approach integrating static and temporal mechanisms
papers.authors: Lu X., Yan Y., Yang G., Xing J.
papers.abstract: Technology convergence is a core engine of innovation. However, most empirical studies rely on static proximity indicators. These static models often overlook topology structure, heterogeneous knowledge attributes, external factors, and temporal path dependence. This study develops a mechanism-oriented dynamic network framework using a Bootstrapped Temporal Exponential Random Graph Model (BTERGM). Based on 16 million USPTO invention patents (2011–2020), we construct annual CPC-4 co-occurrence networks and jointly model four mechanism families: (i) structural properties (sparsity, triadic closure, degree and eigenvector centrality), (ii) semantic proximity captured by CPC hierarchy and text embeddings, (iii) macro-level policy and industry context, and (iv) temporal memory capturing tie persistence, stability, loss, and innovation. Results indicate that structural properties and external drivers operate as independent yet complementary forces shaping convergence. The network is globally sparse but locally cohesive, with strong triadic closure and centrality effects, while semantic proximity remains among the most powerful predictors of tie formation. Funding and industry alignment further tilt convergence toward domains where resources and market demand co-align. Incorporating temporal memory reveals pronounced dyadic inertia—once technologies converge, they are far more likely to remain connected—and improves out-of-sample performance (AUC-PR  ≈ 0.94). Robustness check shows that strong, high-weight ties are especially anchored in structural centrality, external support, and persistence. By integrating multi-dimensional mechanisms within a unified generative framework, this study advances patent-based convergence research and provides a scalable tool for mechanism inference, forecasting, and actionable technology roadmapping.

papers.title: S2CR: A self-supervised self-consistency reasoning framework coupled to retrieval-augmented generation
papers.authors: Shao H., Wang F., Zhang S., Xie Z.
papers.abstract: Existing approaches to the self-consistency exploration in Large Language Models (LLMs) primarily rely on post-hoc selection, overlooking the inherent logical structures essential for reasoning. To address this gap, we pioneer a new perspective by introducing S2CR, a self-supervised reasoning framework that presents the LLM consistency from internal modeling while coupling retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for knowledge integration and process supervision. This framework operates in four stages: Information Retrieval patches the parametric knowledge of LLMs and provides factual grounding for evaluation; Response Generation generates multiple candidate responses for input to explore diverse reasoning paths; Consistency Evaluation quantifies logical consistency by aligning extracted triples from both the generated responses and retrieval information; and Duality Synergy Optimization (DSOP) further bolsters the consistency performance through two complementary modules, Introspection-Driven Self-correction Guidance (IDSG) and Fine-Grained Consensus Alignment (FGCA). Experiments conducted on three public datasets POPQA, Biography, and ALCE-ASQA demonstrate that S2CR achieves objective quantification of internal self-consistency and significantly improves performance ranging from 3.19% to 23.49% over Baseline⋄ across diverse foundational LLMs, e.g., GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, and open-source models LLaMA3-8B and LLaMA3-70B.

papers.title: A framework for developing a text simplification index: Design, validation, visualization
papers.authors: Kapłon R., Piekot T.
papers.abstract: In the rapidly developing field of text simplification, there is a significant gap between the paradigms of machine and manual simplification. Social and regulatory pressure creates a need for rapid and widespread improvement in text comprehensibility, while plain language guidelines (e.g., ISO 24495-1:2023) discourage the use of machine tools and readability metrics. In this paper, we attempt to bridge this gap. We propose the Text Simplification Index (TSI), a new framework for evaluating the degree of text simplification. TSI assesses the similarity of a given text to the key linguistic features of naturally simple and widely read texts. We identified these features by comparing a positive benchmark corpus (3917 online media texts) with a negative one (2160 official texts requiring simplification). To verify the performance of TSI, we conducted a study with 24 experienced plain language experts who were asked to evaluate 21 texts. The correlation between the experts’ judgment and the TSI diagnosis was 0.67—higher than the correlations of other readability formulas. We also verified the possibility of modifying TSI variables during the text simplification process. For this purpose, we conducted a quasi-experiment where 306 domain experts, after a brief plain language course, simplified 14 texts. The results showed that all TSI components can be modified by domain experts, although the degree of improvement for a given feature depends on its type, the expert’s skills, and the text topic. Our framework culminates in the design of a practical infographic that precisely shows authors, editors, and researchers the progress in text simplification across each feature.

papers.title: Dynamic emergency resource allocation via graph attention networks and hierarchical reinforcement learning
papers.authors: Zheng J., Zhao Y., Li Y., Li J., Wang Q.
papers.abstract: The efficient, equitable, and timely allocation of limited emergency resources is critical for enhancing response speed and minimizing losses when confronting diverse, fast-evolving emergencies. This paper investigates a dynamic emergency resource allocation problem (DERAP) that considers fairness, coordination, adaptability, timeliness, and resource insufficiency, and proposes a graph attention network-based hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm (GAT_HRL). Firstly, this paper establishes a mathematical model for the dynamic emergency resource allocation problem, with objectives of fairness, coordination, adaptability, and timeliness. Secondly, the complex multi-dimensional emergency resource allocation information is structured as a heterogeneous graph, and the intricate relationships between resources and demands are mined through Graph Attention Networks (GAT) to capture the state features of resource allocation. Subsequently, the method completes resource and demand allocation decisions separately through the top-level agent and the low-level agent. Finally, experimental validation was conducted across 800 instances across 4 distinct scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior solution performance across all scenarios. Compared with heuristic algorithms and other state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms, the average Gap is improved by a minimum of 2.49% and a maximum of 159.32%. Furthermore, the method exhibits strong scalability—models trained on small-scale datasets generalize effectively to large-scale problems—highlighting its robust generalization capability.

papers.title: ChainCare: Clinical prediction via bidirectional monitoring event chains and multi-event time series modeling
papers.authors: Mu S., Sun Q., Zhang S.
papers.abstract: Clinical prediction based on electronic health records is a key research direction in healthcare, with disease prediction and medication recommendation as its core tasks. Although prior studies have acknowledged the importance of monitoring-level events, such as lab tests and medication administrations, their independent modeling has led most approaches to overlook the event execution logic between these events and to neglect the identification of clinically salient event groups. In this work, we introduce ChainCare, a novel learning framework that, to our knowledge, is the first to jointly model two types of monitoring-level events under a unified representation and explicitly capture their execution logic through bidirectional event chains. Equally importantly, to enable more effective centralized modeling of heterogeneous monitoring events, we propose a hierarchical mechanism that adaptively assigns weights to the unified event set at each time step, allowing the model to identify key event groups and further extract critical visit-level representations from patients’ longitudinal records. These designs jointly enhance the performance of disease prediction and medication recommendation. Extensive experiments on the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our method over state-of-the-art approaches, confirming the effectiveness of modeling event execution logic between monitoring-level events and identifying key event groups. Specifically, ChainCare achieves Jaccard score improvements of 0.8% for disease prediction and 3.3% for medication recommendation on the MIMIC-III dataset, and 0.8% and 7.8% on the MIMIC-IV dataset, respectively. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/guangyunms/ChainCare.

papers.title: Privacy-preserving heterogeneous graph representation learning for recommendation
papers.authors: Wang K., Wang Y., Zhang Z., Deng J., Liu J.
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous information networks (HINs), rich in structural and semantic information, have emerged as an effective paradigm for mitigating data sparsity in recommender systems. However, most existing HIN-based recommender systems rely on centralized data storage, which inevitably poses significant privacy risks. The inherently distributed and structurally complex nature of HINs renders existing privacy-preserving solutions inadequate for such recommendation tasks. To this end, we propose PP-HGRL, a privacy-preserving framework for HIN-based recommendation with formal edge-level differential privacy (DP) guarantees. Specifically, our framework employs a heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) to incorporate heterogeneous relational semantics into user-item interaction modeling, thereby effectively mitigating data sparsity. To protect sensitive interactions in the HIN, we propose a dual-stage DP method that eliminates reliance on trusted third parties and provides privacy protection spanning from data sharing to model deployment. Furthermore, PP-HGRL is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated with various HGNN architectures. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that PP-HGRL outperforms existing state-of-the-art privacy-preserving methods, achieving improvements of up to 12.89 % in Recall and 10.12 % in NDCG under a reasonable privacy budget.

papers.title: Emotion-based song recommendation for mothers with postpartum depression
papers.authors: Vinarti R.A., Fatichin M.R., Widyaningrum D.T.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression is a mental health disorder that can occur in first-time mothers. Music therapy is one of the treatments to help reduce Postpartum Depression (PPD) symptoms and provide sootheness for postpartum mothers. This study aimed to develop an emotion and genre-based music recommendation system designed to meet the emotional needs of mothers with PPD. A music classification model was developed using cochleogram and chromagram-based audio representations to obtain music emotion and genre features through a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) architecture. An evaluation was conducted to assess the effect of using both audio representations on music classification performance. The results show that the use of cochleogram and chromagram-based audio representations, which aims to integrate music spectral and key modulation information, can provide better accuracy compared to other music classifications that only utilizes spectral information. The feature extraction results in the classification process are used to make music recommendations based on similarity between the music emotion and genre information. The result of this study is to provide music recommendations that match the emotional state and preferences of mothers with PPD, as well as contribute to the literature related to audio processing for music classification and recommendation. The user evaluation testing was conducted to 35 new mothers and the satisfaction score result is 65%. Furthermore, subjects claimed that by listening to the recommended music from the app for 5 minutes make them feel more relaxed than before.
